title: Network ACLs
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of network acls and its relationship to AWS Networking and Amazon VPC.
Interpret the example and identify at least one prerequisite or boundary relevant to network acls.
Propose a safe verification or troubleshooting step and record one security, reliability or cost consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn network acls in the context of AWS Networking and Amazon VPC. You will connect the listed subtopics to a practical decision, inspect a small example, and define evidence that would confirm or disprove your assumptions.
content.why_it_matters: Network ACLs matters because it is one part of amazon vpc and network reachability. Real workloads depend on explicit prerequisites, correct permissions, predictable behavior and a way to verify outcomes. Learning the decision points helps you distinguish a working demonstration from a safe and supportable design.

content_blocks.title: VPC routing and network controls
content_blocks.alt_text: Reachability combines subnet routing, a route target, addressability, security groups, network ACLs and service-specific controls.
content_blocks.caption: A route alone does not prove reachability; all relevant network and identity controls matter.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** Network ACLs belongs to AWS Networking and Amazon VPC. VPC reachability is an end-to-end result of address ranges, subnet associations, routes, gateways, security groups, network ACLs and service endpoints—not just one firewall rule.

The PDF lists these subtopics: Network ACL fundamentals; Stateless filtering; Rule ordering; Network ACLs versus security groups. Treat them as a connected workflow rather than a list to memorize. Start with the workload requirement, identify the AWS resource/control involved, and write down who owns configuration and operation.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: **Apply it safely.** For network acls, name the prerequisites and the expected result before making a change. Prefer a read-only inspection or local/static example first. Then plan a normal case, a failure case, and a verification step. In a live account, require the account owner-approved sandbox, narrow permissions, spend visibility and cleanup plan. Do not put credentials in code or commit local configuration files.

items.title: Network ACL fundamentals
items.text: Trace the path from source to destination through address ranges, routing, gateways and filtering controls. Verify both forward and return paths; one successful configuration screen is not proof of reachability.

items.title: Stateless filtering
items.text: Compare the available option with the workload requirement; record the operational, security, availability and cost trade-offs rather than assuming one option is always best.

items.title: Rule ordering
items.text: Write a verification step and a failure case. For hands-on work, start with read-only inspection and use an approved sandbox before changing cloud resources.

items.title: Network ACLs versus security groups
items.text: State the principal, action, resource and applicable conditions. Prefer scoped permissions and temporary credentials, protect secrets, and collect evidence that access is both limited and usable.

content_blocks.title: Security group versus network ACL
content_blocks.code:
Security group: stateful, attached to network interfaces, allow rules
Network ACL: stateless, associated with subnets, numbered allow/deny rules
content_blocks.expected_output: Return traffic and rule order differ; troubleshoot the packet path in both directions.

content_blocks.title: Security and cost checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use least privilege, keep Block Public Access/private defaults unless a justified reviewed requirement says otherwise, and document cost/cleanup before live changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one successful example as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: The example may not test permissions, regional/service prerequisites, retries, recovery, quotas or edge cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Write acceptance criteria, test a failure path, inspect logs/state and record the limits of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing a live resource before confirming its effect and cost.
common_mistakes.why: Cloud changes can expose data, break traffic or leave billable dependencies behind.
common_mistakes.fix: Start read-only, use an approved sandbox, review the change, tag ownership and verify cleanup.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying broad permissions or credentials into source files.
common_mistakes.why: Broad permissions and leaked long-lived credentials increase the impact of mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Use scoped roles/temporary credentials, keep secrets in approved stores and review access boundaries.

summary: Network ACLs is taught as part of AWS Networking and Amazon VPC.
VPC reachability is an end-to-end result of address ranges, subnet associations, routes, gateways, security groups, network ACLs and service endpoints—not just one firewall rule.
Verify assumptions with official service documentation and evidence from the relevant AWS resource, logs or tests.
For live labs, confirm permissions and likely charges before acting, then verify cleanup.
